items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mitchell Ayres was the bandleader. I was the first black musician to be in the band on ABC

ctx.x: We left off with your early studio years and I want to get back to that and explore that area. When you first came out to Los Angeles, you were just mentioning the barriers in classical music, well the barriers in studio work were pretty rigid at that time. How did you first break into the, I don’t mean going on staff, but even getting calls, how did that first come about and who were some of the conductors that were more open to having black musicians work with them?

Well, the Hollywood Palace, ABC, and I think that they were looking for somebody. It didn’t have to be me, just thank God it was me. And I was blessed. Mitchell Ayres was the bandleader. I was the first black musician to be in the band on ABC and the time was just right. I think they were looking for a black musician.

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: I did the Hollywood Palace show for three years with Mitchell Ayresand the experience I got there playing was just absolutely fantastic.

ctx.x: And so I finally -- San Francisco, when we came back from Europe, we just did one-nighters, and I just -- I hated to leave, so I just took my uniform, put it in the bus and split. I didn't even want to say goodbye or anything, you know. Then I came back to California and I assumed my studio work out here. I did the Hollywood Palace show for three years with Mitchell Ayresand the experience I got there playing was just absolutely fantastic.
How did that differ from what you'd done with Nelson Riddle ?

items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I got a studio job here at ABC, with Mitchell Ayres on the Hollywood Palace

ctx.x: How many years did you spend with the Basie band?

Well from ‘38 until 1950, then I went back and I got a studio job here at ABC, with Mitchell Ayres on the Hollywood Palace, and then I started playing with Frank Sinatra. I did everything with him and Nelson Riddle for about 13 years. I recorded a lot with Nat King Cole, Ella Fitzgerald. I’ve been blessed all my life. It seems like that I don’t know why I’ve been called to do records that like anybody could have done it you know.

Yeah, but like you stated, you had your sound. You must have developed a sound that people recognized and that when Frank Sinatra did a date, he knew who he wanted to hear behind him, as did Nelson Riddle.
